question.text: In the anion $\mathrm{HCOO}^{-}$ the two carbon-oxygen bonds are found to be of equal length. What is the reason for it?

options.text: The $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$ bond is weaker than the $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}$ bond.
The anion $\mathrm{HCOO}^{-}$ has two resonating structures.
The anion is obtained byremoval of a proton from the acid molecule.
Electronic orbitals of carbon atom are hybridised.
